questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Matters
This question assesses the ability to design a secure, scalable, multi-tenant Azure architecture that addresses isolation, cross-tenant management, governance, and automated infrastructure deployment.

## Key Concepts
- Multi-tenant architecture with logical and network isolation
- Azure Lighthouse for cross-tenant delegated access management
- Private Link and VNet integration for data-plane security
- Terraform with GitHub Actions for Infrastructure as Code
- Azure Policy and budgets for governance and cost enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions: Terraform CI/CD Pipeline
name: Terraform CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  terraform:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      
      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
      
      - name: Terraform Format Check
        run: terraform fmt -check
      
      - name: Terraform Init
        run: terraform init
      
      - name: Terraform Validate
        run: terraform validate
      
      - name: Terraform Plan
        run: terraform plan
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
      
      - name: Terraform Apply
        run: terraform apply -auto-approve
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
```

questions.explanation:
## Architecture Overview

### Data Ingestion
- Event Hubs with Private Link endpoints connect each partner's virtual network
- Each partner gets their own namespace or consumer group for logical separation
- Data is partitioned by tenant ID to maintain ordered processing per partner

### Storage & Isolation
- Single Gen2 storage account with folder structure: `/tenants/{tenant_id}/`
- Access Control Lists (ACLs) at folder level use security groups linked to partner Azure AD identities
- NOT separate storage accounts (too expensive, harder to manage, defeats Data Lake benefits)
- Customer-managed keys in Key Vault encrypt all data at rest

### Security & Governance
- RBAC controls access at subscription and resource group levels
- Managed Identities authenticate Spark jobs to access Data Lake
- Azure Lighthouse enables cross-tenant operations with delegated permissions
- Microsoft Purview catalogs and governs all data assets

### CI/CD Pipeline
- GitHub Actions deploys infrastructure using Terraform
- Spark jobs are packaged and deployed via Synapse Linked Service updates

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This scenario tests practical Azure fundamentals: streaming ingestion, cross-region disaster recovery, private networking, identity management, cost governance, and CI/CD for infrastructure-as-code. It also evaluates the ability to balance latency requirements with regional locality and budget constraints.

## Key Concepts
- **Event Hubs Standard** with auto-inflate for elastic throughput
- **Databricks Structured Streaming** for near real-time processing
- **Synapse DW** with private endpoints for secure data warehousing
- **Entra ID** and RBAC for identity-driven access control
- **Azure Private Link** for private endpoint connectivity
- **RA-GRS** storage with geo-DR alias for disaster recovery
- Cost governance through budgets and right-sizing
- GitHub Actions for IaC validation and deployment

## Architecture Overview
The mobile-game telemetry pipeline sends events to Event Hubs in Region A. A Databricks job continuously reads, aggregates on an hourly basis, and writes to Synapse DW. Private endpoints ensure all network traffic stays within the virtual network. For DR, enable RA-GRS on the storage account and use a geo-DR alias to fail over to Region B if Region A becomes unavailable.

## Cost-Conscious Considerations
- Use Event Hubs auto-inflate to scale throughput only when needed
- Choose appropriate Synapse DW performance tier for workload
- Implement budgets and alerts to monitor spending
- Leverage Reserved Instances for predictable workloads

## GitHub Actions Workflow
```yaml
name: IaC Validation
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate ARM templates
        run: |-
          az deployment group validate ...
      - name: Check Terraform
        run: terraform validate
      - name: Lint Bicep
        run: az bicep build --file main.bicep
```
